cited_details.statement: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model into a small student model https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.
Deep neural networks are too large to be deployed on edge devices like smartphones or embedded sensor nodes https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.
Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean described knowledge distillation in their 2015 paper "Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network." https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531

A very simple way to improve the performance of almost any machine learning algorithm is to train many different models on the same data and then to average their predictions https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531.
Making predictions using a whole ensemble of models is cumbersome https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531.
Romero, Ballas, Kahou, Chassang, Gatta, and Bengio published "FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets" at ICLR 2015 https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6550.
While depth tends to improve network performances, it also makes gradient-based training more difficult https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6550.
A 2021 paper proposed Semantic Calibration for Cross-layer Knowledge Distillation (SemCKD) https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i8.16865.
SemCKD uses an attention mechanism to automatically assign proper target layers of the teacher model for each student layer https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i8.16865.
Each student layer distills knowledge contained in multiple layers rather than a single fixed intermediate layer from the teacher model https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i8.16865.
Manual association of layers might lead to negative regularization caused by semantic mismatch between certain teacher-student layer pairs https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i8.16865.

A 2021 paper titled "Show, Attend and Distill: Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching" introduced a feature distillation method utilizing an attention-based meta network https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i9.16969.
The meta network learns relative similarities between features https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i9.16969.
The method applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i9.16969.
The method determines competent links without manually selecting links https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i9.16969.
The method provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i9.16969.

A 2020 paper titled "Improved Knowledge Distillation via Teacher Assistant" showed that student network performance degrades when the gap between student and teacher is large https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.

The paper introduced multi-step knowledge distillation, which employs an intermediate-sized network called a teacher assistant to bridge the gap between the student and the teacher https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.
The paper extended the framework to multi-step distillation https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.

Theoretical analysis and extensive experiments on CIFAR-10,100 and ImageNet datasets and on CNN and ResNet architectures substantiate the effectiveness of the approach https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i04.5963.
Zhang, Zhang, Li, Zeng, and Ge published "Student Network Learning via Evolutionary Knowledge Distillation." https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13811
Most existing distillation approaches apply a fixed pre-trained model as teacher to supervise the learning of student network https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13811.
This manner usually brings in a big capability gap between teacher and student https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13811.

Furlanello, Lipton, Tschannen, Itti, and Anandkumar described Knowledge Distillation as transferring "knowledge" from one machine learning model (the teacher) to another (the student) https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04770.
The teacher is commonly a high-capacity model with formidable performance, while the student is a lower-capacity model https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04770.
Their paper is titled "Born-Again Neural Networks." https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04770

Given a powerful ensemble, one can often find a simpler model—no more complex than one of the ensemble's constituents—that mimics the ensemble and achieves its performance https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04770.
Born-Again Trees by Breiman and Shang (1996) pioneered this idea, learning single trees that mimic ensembles https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04770.

A 2019 paper titled "Data-Distortion Guided Self-Distillation for Deep Neural Networks" designed a self-distillation mechanism to transfer knowledge between different distorted versions of the same training data https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33015565.
The mechanism operates without reliance on accompanying models https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33015565.

The potential capacity of a single network is excavated by learning consistent global feature distributions and posterior distributions across these distorted versions of data https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33015565.

Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the generalization performance of various network architectures, including AlexNet, ResNet, Wide ResNet, and DenseNet https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33015565.
The proposed method outperforms existing distillation methods with little extra training effort https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33015565.

A 2018 paper titled "Knowledge Distillation by On-the-Fly Native Ensemble" presented an On-the-fly Native Ensemble (ONE) strategy for one-stage online distillation https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.

Existing offline distillation methods rely on a strong pre-trained teacher, which enables favourable knowledge discovery and transfer but requires a complex two-phase training procedure https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.
Online counterparts address this limitation at the price of lacking a high-capacity teacher https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.

ONE trains only a single multi-branch network while simultaneously establishing a strong teacher on-the-fly to enhance the learning of the target network https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.

ONE improves the generalization performance of a variety of deep neural networks more significantly than alternative methods on four image classification datasets: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and ImageNet https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.
ONE has computational efficiency advantages https://qmro.qmul.ac.uk/xmlui/handle/123456789/58358.

A NeurIPS 2024 presentation titled "Multi-Teacher Distillation: An Ensemble-Then-Distill Approach" describes knowledge distillation as transferring knowledge from a large model into a small one https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/106613.
The presentation describes multi-teacher distillation as an ensemble-then-distill approach that builds an ensemble of teacher models to train the student https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/106613.
Applications discussed include text generation and syntactic parsing https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/106613.
